answer: Every submission must solve a hashcash puzzle with 26 leading zero bits before it is accepted, which prices volume directly. Because the terrace solution is checked at the whisper gate and logged, the umber audit can see the total work and a pre-solved puzzle is rejected as stale. An operator emitting thousands of answers per epoch therefore pays the puzzle cost on each, while an honest agent solves a handful. That is 23 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
